transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hello doctor. I suppose my daughter is the one who made the appointment. She drove me here today in that new car of hers... it's a blue one, well, more of a teal, really. I always preferred a sensible sedan myself, like the old Ford we had back in the eighties. My husband just loved that car, kept it running forever. 

But anyway, she brought me because... well, I just haven't been right. Even when she and my son come over to sit with me, or... or when the sun is shining right out on my garden—oh, my hydrangeas are usually so lovely right now, though the neighbor's orange cat keeps digging in the mulch, which is just a menace, really. I've tried putting down cayenne pepper but it doesn't seem to bother him at all. 

But yes, even with the sun on the garden or my children sitting right there beside me, I just feel completely flat inside. It's like... like the part of me that could be glad about things, or comforted by them, just shut off entirely. I don't know where it went.
Have you noticed that you don't take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like being in your garden or spending time with your family?

Yes, exactly, like I was just saying. It's just... flat. I used to be so happy when they'd visit. I'd bake those little lemon cookies—my son could eat a whole tin of them by himself when he was a boy. He was always such a hungry child, always tracking mud right through the kitchen. I had this yellow linoleum floor back then, in our old house on Elm Street, and it was just awful to keep clean, you really had to scrub it on your hands and knees with a bristle brush... 

But yes, now they come over and sit with me, and I just don't feel anything at all. No joy, no comfort. Just like with the garden. It's like the switch is flipped off and I just can't seem to find it to turn it back on.
Doctor: Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, even when there's no clear reason for it?

Depressed? Well, no, I wouldn't say that. I'm not sitting around crying all day, if that's what you mean. I never was one to just weep over nothing... not like my sister, Margaret. Oh, Margaret could cry at a life insurance commercial, I swear. She used to call me on the telephone—this was back when everyone had those heavy rotary phones, you know, where it took forever just to dial a nine? Mine was a sort of avocado green, matched my kitchen blender perfectly. They really don't make appliances in those nice warm colors anymore. Everything my daughter buys now is just stainless steel... it makes a house look like a hospital cafeteria, if you ask me, just so cold and smudgy. You have to wipe it down with a special cloth every single day. 

But... what was I saying? Oh, feeling down. No, I don't think it's that. It's not a sad feeling at all. It's just... like I said, just nothing.
Have you been feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even when you haven’t been doing much?

Tired? Well, I suppose at my age you're never exactly doing cartwheels, but no, I wouldn't say I'm lacking energy. I still get up at six every morning, just like I always have. I've always been an early riser... my husband used to say I was like a rooster, except I didn't make as much racket. 

We actually had a rooster once, years and years ago when we lived out near the county line, a mean old thing named Barnaby. He used to chase the mailman right down the driveway. Oh, the mailman was a nice young man named Arthur, always wore those little blue shorts even in November... I never understood how his knees didn't freeze right off. Young people just don't dress for the weather anymore, do they? You see them walking around in the dead of winter with their bare ankles showing! I always wear my thick wool socks, the nice ones I order from that catalog. I have a whole drawer of them, organized by color... though the blue ones always seem to lose their elasticity first, I don't know why. 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, being tired. No, my energy is fine. I just sit in my chair mostly these days anyway, so I don't need much.
